# tests/fixtures/live_cells -- the red half of every regression cell

[Co-developed with claude code -- Adam]

One directory per cell in `tools/test_workflow/live_cells/`, and up to three things in it:

| | what it is |
|---|---|
| `old/` | the raw a **pre-fix** run produced. `<cell>.sh judge old/` must FAIL. This is the cell's red, and it is the only reason the cell counts as delivered -- a judge nobody has seen fail is a decoration (CLAUDE.md). |
| `new/` | the raw the **first fixed** run produced. `judge new/` must PASS. |
| `old/EXPECTED-FAILS` | the exact assert ids that fail on `old/`, one per line, **reviewed by hand**. `tests/shell/mutate_live_cells.sh` compares the failing set against this file, so removing an assertion from a judge changes the set and the gate goes red. It is NOT regenerated by the gate: a file the gate writes is a file the gate cannot check. |
| `old/PROVENANCE.md` | where every byte of `old/` came from, and -- when the old evidence is thinner than the judge -- which of the failing assertions carry the finding and which merely fail because a file was never kept. |

## 🔴 Three rules about `old/`

1. **It is last night's evidence, or it is a replay of a pre-fix tool, and PROVENANCE says which.**
   A directory somebody wrote by hand to make a judge go red would grade the instrument against
   itself. The two honest kinds are: files copied out of a round's logs (colour codes stripped,
   only the files the judge reads), and files produced by running the tool as it was at
   `<fix commit>^`. Both are recorded per file.
2. **A failing assertion is not automatically the finding.** Several `old/` directories are
   thinner than their cell's raw layout, because the role that measured the defect did not keep
   every file the cell now writes -- ROLE-6 kept no `up.target`, ROLE-2's cycle probe kept only
   the `VERDICT:` line. Those assertions fail with `no such raw file`, which is honest but is a
   fixture gap and not evidence. Each PROVENANCE.md names the assertions that carry the finding,
   and the gate mutates only those.
3. **A cell with no `new/` yet is PENDING, not passing.** The gate says so, on its own line, and
   counts it separately.
